description: Fig. 5 is a vertically stacked set of four conventional X-ray diffraction patterns of the same Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel after successive multiaxial forging (MAF) passes, labelled MAF-0 (bottom, solution-treated), MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 (top). All four share one horizontal axis, 2θ (degree), running 40 to 120° with major ticks every 20°; the vertical axis is Intensity (count), but each panel is drawn on its own scale — 0-7500 count (MAF-0), 0-2460 (MAF-1), 0-1050 (MAF-3) and 0-870 (MAF-5) — so absolute peak heights cannot be compared directly between panels. Only face-centred-cubic austenite reflections dominate: the MAF-0 trace is labelled γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), κ(220), γ(311) and γ(222), while MAF-1 additionally labels weak δ(211) and κ(222) features near 95-105° 2θ. No scale bar or inset is present. With increasing pass number the reflections broaden and their relative heights change: γ(111) near 50° 2θ is the strongest line at MAF-0, whereas from MAF-1 upward the high-angle γ(220) line near 87° 2θ is tallest. The figure therefore demonstrates that MAF introduces lattice microstrain/grain refinement (peak broadening) and a change in preferred orientation (texture) in an otherwise single-phase austenitic steel, while the carbide reflections remain.

observations.observation: The figure consists of four vertically stacked XRD patterns labelled MAF-0, MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 from bottom to top.
The horizontal axis of every pattern is 2θ (degree) from 40 to 120 with major ticks at 20° intervals; the vertical axis is Intensity (count).
Each pattern uses a different intensity scale: 0-7500 count (MAF-0), 0-2460 (MAF-1), 0-1050 (MAF-3) and 0-870 (MAF-5), so peak heights are not directly comparable between panels.
The MAF-0 pattern carries the peak labels γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), κ(220), γ(311) and γ(222).
The MAF-1 pattern carries the additional labels δ(211) and κ(222) on weak features near 95-105° 2θ.
In MAF-0 the γ(111) line near 50° 2θ is the most intense, whereas from MAF-1 upward the γ(220) line near 87° 2θ has the greatest height.
Peaks in the MAF-3 and MAF-5 patterns appear broader than in MAF-0 and MAF-1.
The caption states that the figure presents XRD patterns at different MAF passes.

The citing text states that there is no difference between the carbides before and after the MAF pass as illustrated by the X-ray patterns in Fig. 5, so carbide precipitation strengthening is treated as constant.
The citing text states that the examined Fe-Mn-Al-C steels contain only the majority austenite phase, consistent with the γ-labelled reflections dominating every pattern.
The citing text attributes the change in intensity and broadening of the peaks with increasing forging passes to grain-size refinement and increased lattice strain.
The citing text interprets the change from the highest intensity (111) in the solutioned sample to (220) at MAF-1 as evidence of texturing.

The citing text states that lattice microstrain and crystallite size were determined from the average peak broadening of all FCC peaks using a Williamson-Hall plot (values given in Table 1), and that the Burgers vector b is 0.259 nm.
The citing text states that dislocation density is estimated from the XRD-measured microstrain (Fig. 5) and used to predict yield strength after each MAF pass.

subfigures.description: XRD pattern of the solution-treated (0-pass) sample plotted as Intensity (count), 0-7500, versus 2θ = 40-120°. Strong sharp lines labelled γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), with weaker κ(220), γ(311) and γ(222); γ(111) near 50° 2θ is the most intense peak.

XRD pattern of the 1-pass sample, Intensity (count) 0-2460 versus 2θ = 40-120°. Two dominant sharp peaks (near 51° and 87° 2θ, the latter tallest) plus low-intensity features labelled δ(211) and κ(222) near 95-105° 2θ.

XRD pattern of the 3-pass sample, Intensity (count) 0-1050 versus 2θ = 40-120°. Peaks are broader and weaker than in MAF-0; a strong line near 87° 2θ and a lower one near 51° 2θ, with minor unlabelled features near 63-65° and 95-110° 2θ.

XRD pattern of the 5-pass sample, Intensity (count) 0-870 versus 2θ = 40-120°. Similar peak positions to MAF-3 (near 51° and 87° 2θ) with further broadening; minor high-angle features are unlabelled and barely above background.

unreadable_items: minor unlabelled peaks near 63-65° 2θ in the MAF-3 and MAF-5 patterns cannot be assigned
the weak δ(211)/κ(222) features in MAF-1 are close to the noise level and their exact positions cannot be read accurately
high-angle features above 100° 2θ in the MAF-3 and MAF-5 patterns are too weak to assign
